questions.stem: This H&E-stained myocardial biopsy shows myocytes separated by expanded pale-staining fibrocollagenous tissue. This histologic pattern of interstitial infiltration/fibrosis stiffening the ventricular wall is the hallmark of which cardiomyopathy?

explanation.summary: Restrictive cardiomyopathy is characterized by increased ventricular wall stiffness from interstitial fibrosis or infiltration between myocytes, impairing diastolic filling while systolic function is often preserved.
explanation.whyCorrect: Restrictive cardiomyopathy is characterized by increased ventricular wall stiffness from interstitial fibrosis or infiltration between myocytes, impairing diastolic filling while systolic function is often preserved.

questions.stem: The left panel shows myocardium stained with a special dye, and the right panel shows the same field under polarized light where the deposits display apple-green birefringence. Which material is being demonstrated?

explanation.summary: Congo red stains amyloid, which shows pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light due to the beta-pleated sheet structure. This confirms cardiac amyloidosis as the cause of restrictive cardiomyopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Congo red stains amyloid, which shows pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light due to the beta-pleated sheet structure. This confirms cardiac amyloidosis as the cause of restrictive cardiomyopathy.

questions.stem: This myocardial section is stained with a histochemical dye that turns intracellular deposits bright blue. In a patient with restrictive cardiomyopathy, diabetes, and bronze skin, what does the blue reaction identify?

explanation.summary: The Prussian blue (Perls) reaction stains ferric iron blue. Myocardial iron overload in hereditary hemochromatosis or transfusional siderosis causes a restrictive/dilated cardiomyopathy; the triad of diabetes, skin pigmentation, and organ deposition is classic.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Prussian blue (Perls) reaction stains ferric iron blue. Myocardial iron overload in hereditary hemochromatosis or transfusional siderosis causes a restrictive/dilated cardiomyopathy; the triad of diabetes, skin pigmentation, and organ deposition is classic.

questions.stem: This cardiac imaging study (arrows indicating myocardial signal abnormality) is increasingly used to characterize infiltrative cardiomyopathies noninvasively, using late gadolinium enhancement and tissue mapping. Which modality is shown?

explanation.summary: Cardiac MRI provides tissue characterization; late gadolinium enhancement patterns and T1/T2 mapping help identify infiltrative and inflammatory causes of restrictive cardiomyopathy such as amyloid, sarcoid, and fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac MRI provides tissue characterization; late gadolinium enhancement patterns and T1/T2 mapping help identify infiltrative and inflammatory causes of restrictive cardiomyopathy such as amyloid, sarcoid, and fibrosis.

questions.stem: This H&E section of myocardium from a patient with restrictive physiology shows cardiomyocytes separated and surrounded by abundant pale, amorphous, acellular pink interstitial material. Which deposition process does this most likely represent?

explanation.summary: Cardiac amyloidosis deposits amorphous, eosinophilic, acellular protein in the interstitium and around myocytes, stiffening the ventricle and producing a restrictive cardiomyopathy with impaired diastolic filling.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac amyloidosis deposits amorphous, eosinophilic, acellular protein in the interstitium and around myocytes, stiffening the ventricle and producing a restrictive cardiomyopathy with impaired diastolic filling.

questions.stem: This myocardial biopsy shows a focal collection of epithelioid histiocytes and mixed inflammatory cells forming a granuloma surrounded by scarring, in a patient with heart block and restrictive physiology. Which infiltrative disease is most likely?

explanation.summary: Cardiac sarcoidosis produces noncaseating granulomas in the myocardium that can cause conduction blocks, arrhythmias, and a restrictive/infiltrative cardiomyopathy. Granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid histiocytes distinguishes it from bland fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac sarcoidosis produces noncaseating granulomas in the myocardium that can cause conduction blocks, arrhythmias, and a restrictive/infiltrative cardiomyopathy. Granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid histiocytes distinguishes it from bland fibrosis.

questions.stem: This gross four-chamber section of the heart shows markedly dilated left and right atria with non-dilated ventricles of relatively normal wall thickness. This atrial-predominant enlargement is the classic morphologic signature of which condition?

explanation.summary: Restrictive cardiomyopathy produces stiff ventricles with impaired diastolic filling; chronically elevated filling pressures dilate both atria while the ventricles remain normal in size. Marked biatrial enlargement with normal-sized ventricles is the hallmark gross finding.
explanation.whyCorrect: Restrictive cardiomyopathy produces stiff ventricles with impaired diastolic filling; chronically elevated filling pressures dilate both atria while the ventricles remain normal in size. Marked biatrial enlargement with normal-sized ventricles is the hallmark gross finding.

questions.stem: Comparing the two labeled diagrams of the heart, the abnormal one on the right has a stiffened ventricular wall with preserved chamber size. What is the primary hemodynamic consequence of this change?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduced systolic contractility with a dilated ventricle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Impaired diastolic filling with preserved systolic function

explanation.summary: In restrictive cardiomyopathy the myocardium becomes stiff and non-compliant, limiting diastolic filling and raising filling pressures while ejection fraction is initially preserved. This causes biatrial enlargement and signs of right- and left-sided congestion.
explanation.whyCorrect: In restrictive cardiomyopathy the myocardium becomes stiff and non-compliant, limiting diastolic filling and raising filling pressures while ejection fraction is initially preserved. This causes biatrial enlargement and signs of right- and left-sided congestion.
